title: Cover Picture and Issue Information
content:
Common toads, like many other amphibian species, are nocturnal and thus particularly exposed to nocturnal light pollution. A growing number of studies reveal the negative impact that it has on both their behaviour and physiology (Credit: Louise Cheynel).

This month’s cover image is provided by the authors of ‘Does nocturnal light pollution impair immune function in a wild-living amphibian?’ (https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2435.70212), which features in this issue. They assessed whether the effects of light pollution on immunity previously reported in experimental studies were also observable in 15 natural populations of common toads. Their study emphasises the need for more studies on the effect of light pollution on physiology in natural conditions of exposure, and its interactions with other anthropogenic perturbations, to be able to truly understand its effects on wildlife.
